body:
#90 is merged. It adds the test this issue asks for and logs that show where commit time goes.

The `stress` job in ci runs `TestLargeValuesAtRealTicks` 20 times for 10 s each, with 100 ms ticks and two clients per node writing 1.5 MiB values. A put that takes over 1 s on the wall clock fails it, and so does a leader entry that waits one election timeout. Both reviewers checked that it fails when they inject a 1.1 to 1.2 s stall into the disk or the committer.

On #90's runs, all 20 repetitions passed both before and after the review fixes. So the stall has not reproduced at real ticks yet, and its cause is still unknown. I am leaving this issue open. The job runs on every PR, so if it fails, the node logs (slow log writes, leader and term changes, peer queue waits) will name where the time went.
